messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Minecraft-like 3D game for phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- “Create a game like minecraft (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)”
- Build it now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created a browser-based voxel sandbox called “Wildfern” with touch and desktop controls.
- Used Three.js from jsDelivr; gameplay focuses on a small meadow with mining, placing, inventory, movement, and jumping.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive game shell, intro/pause UI, hotbar, and mobile controls.
- Implemented procedural voxel island, trees, flowers, water, block selection, mining/placing, inventory, and movement.
- Served locally at `http://localhost:3002`; browser confirmed the Three.js scene renders.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/wildfern-intro.jpg` and `screenshots/wildfern-play.jpg`.
- Syntax and whitespace checks passed before the latest small changes.

### Active
- Final browser verification after the latest camera orientation, touch-device detection, CSS, and favicon changes.
- Check `game.js` syntax and `git diff --check` again.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Reload the page, test desktop gameplay and a mobile viewport/touch controls, and save/read the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Review git status; changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game markup and UI.
- `style.css`: responsive layout and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player, inventory, and interactions.
- `screenshots/wildfern-play.jpg`: latest gameplay screenshot, captured before the final camera/control edits.

## Important Context
- `playwright-cli` initially failed because Chromium was missing; Chromium was installed and the browser opened successfully afterward.
- Local HTTP server was started in tmux session `wildfern`, serving port 3002.
- Last browser check showed the scene rendering, but view angle was adjusted afterward to face the island; the final edits have not yet been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Minecraft-like 3D game for phones and tablets.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification, make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created “Wildfern,” a browser-based voxel sandbox using Three.js from jsDelivr.
- Gameplay centers on a meadow with mining, placing, inventory, movement, jumping, and mobile touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added responsive game shell, intro/pause UI, hotbar, and mobile controls.
- Implemented procedural voxel island, trees, flowers, water, block selection, mining/placing, inventory, movement, and jumping.
- Started local server at `http://localhost:3002`; browser confirmed the Three.js scene renders.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/wildfern-intro.jpg` and `screenshots/wildfern-play.jpg`.

### Active
- Verify the latest camera orientation, touch-device detection, CSS, and favicon changes in desktop and mobile browser views.
- Re-run JavaScript syntax and whitespace checks; review git status.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `node --input-type=module --check < game.js` and `git diff --check`.
2. Reload the page, test desktop gameplay and a mobile viewport/touch controls, and save/read the latest JPEG screenshot.
3. Review git status; changes are uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game markup, UI, and inline favicon.
- `style.css`: responsive layout and touch controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player, inventory, and interactions.
- `screenshots/wildfern-play.jpg`: gameplay screenshot; captured before the latest camera/control edits.

## Important Context
- `playwright-cli` initially failed because Chromium was missing; Chromium was installed and the browser opened successfully afterward.
- The latest edits have not yet been verified in-browser.
